summary: Verified the AttachmentsCard open-attachment fix on WEB as OWNER on /bookings/bk_4936b1b2ab. Card shows the 2 seeded attachments (lab-report.pdf chip + xray.png thumbnail). Tapping the PDF chip triggered a real file download of the decoded blob (a6ebdbcc-...pdf, i.e. window.open on blob URL that the browser served as a download / anchor-download fallback fired). Tapping the image thumbnail opened a NEW browser tab whose URL is a proper blob: object URL (blob:https://urology-pro.preview.emergentagent.com/2ac5f67a-...). No blank popup, no anti-navigation on the data: URL — the reported regression is fixed. Zero JS console errors were emitted during the two open actions. Native / installed-app behaviour (expo-sharing) cannot be exercised in this web-preview environment, per the request — not attempted.

issues: Each attachment footer shows '0 KB · primary_owner' because the seeded files are 197 B and 70 B — (a.size/1024).toFixed(0) rounds sub-KB files to 0. Consider showing '<1 KB' or bytes for tiny files. Cosmetic only.
The 70-byte xray.png thumbnail renders as a solid black rectangle (its base64 is not a valid image body). Purely a seed-data artefact — not a code bug — but a real patient upload would look fine.

action_items: No fix required for the reported bug — the AttachmentsCard.openFile() web path (Blob + URL.createObjectURL + window.open with anchor-download fallback) works: PDF triggered a download of decoded bytes, image opened in a new tab at a blob: URL, and no console errors were produced.

(Optional cosmetic) In AttachmentsCard.tsx line 314, replace `(a.size/1024).toFixed(0) KB` with a size formatter that shows bytes for sub-KB files (`< 1 KB` or `197 B`), so tiny report chips don't display as '0 KB'.
critical_code_review_comments: AttachmentsCard now correctly imports 'expo-file-system/legacy' — required because the modern expo-file-system (v19) no longer exports writeAsStringAsync / readAsStringAsync / cacheDirectory. Keep the /legacy suffix until the code is migrated to the new File/Directory API.
Web open path is defensive: catches atob failures, falls back from window.open → anchor download, revokes the object URL after 60s. Good.
readAssetBase64 correctly branches on Platform.OS === 'web' and reads via FileReader (fixing the silent PDF-upload failure on browsers).
openFile still calls Alert.alert on failure paths — fine on native, but on web Alert renders inline; acceptable.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Playwright popup/download listeners are the right way to assert AttachmentsCard.openFile on web — attach page.on('popup') AND page.on('download') because a blob: window.open for a PDF is often handled by Chromium as a download (that's why the PDF click showed a download event, and the image click showed a proper blob: popup URL). Both count as 'opened'. To reproduce: localStorage.setItem('session_token','test_session_1781800271528') then visit /bookings/bk_4936b1b2ab. Native / installed-app open-via-Sharing was NOT exercised here (out of environment scope).
rca_of_issue: Root cause of the original bug: (1) On web, the previous implementation navigated top-level to a data: URL, which modern browsers block for cross-origin/top-frame navigations — hence the blank popup that immediately closed. (2) On native, the previous implementation called FileSystem.writeAsStringAsync / cacheDirectory from the modern expo-file-system v19 module, which no longer exports those symbols (moved to a File/Directory API), so the call threw TypeError and the tap did nothing. Fix verified: web now builds a Blob from atob(content_base64), calls URL.createObjectURL, and window.open's the blob URL (with an anchor-download fallback); native imports 'expo-file-system/legacy' whose surface still has writeAsStringAsync/cacheDirectory + hands the file to expo-sharing. Web verification passed; native path cannot be exercised in this preview but the legacy import + Sharing.shareAsync pattern is standard.
